**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Anchor the migration to an ancestor of this release**

For release SHA `7e78303ac3ea0c9ce025d7ea4edab5d03d81b8fa`, `441dfcc968559f829e84c89751f008657566138c` is not an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` returns false). The guarded release path in `scripts/production-release.mjs` checks every `introducedBy` commit and explicitly refuses such a release, so planning or deploying this exact commit will fail before applying the migration. Record an introduction commit that is actually in this release's ancestry.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Verified on 697bd58b5ea1c8134be490cce588b65e9a08dad8: introduction commit 441dfcc968559f829e84c89751f008657566138c is in the current release ancestry. All 115 registered introduction commits pass git merge-base --is-ancestor, and all 82 production-release tests pass. The earlier review snapshot is superseded by the existing normal commits; no ancestry guard or manifest entry was weakened. Native-stack automatic rebasing has not been invoked.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include discovery events in the pilot status count**

This function makes structured imports consume the same 20-item allowance as research candidates, but `loadPilotDTO` in `TDF.Server.EventResearch` still computes `erPilotActiveCandidates` solely from `event_research_candidate`. For example, with 19 candidates and one imported event, `GET /social-events/event-research/pilot` reports 19 of 20 while the next candidate is rejected by this trigger. Clients following the documented preflight therefore receive a misleading capacity value; derive the status count from the shared identities (or expose a separate shared count).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 697bd58b5ea1c8134be490cce588b65e9a08dad8. The pilot-status endpoint and PostgreSQL import preflight now call the same canonical-identity count used by the database capacity guard. The real PostgreSQL regression exercises mixed candidates/imports, linked-event deduplication, duplicate source references and suppression (20 → 20 → 19 → 20), with fixture changes rolled back. Mixed-writer races, authority/revocation and rollback/reapplication still pass; all 28 focused examples and the actual handler/dependency compilation pass. The existing response field is retained for compatibility.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Abort reconciliation when the source is disabled**

When an administrator disables a source after its fetch begins, this new check makes each per-event sync fail, but `syncOne` catches those failures and `runDiscoverySource` still reaches the success branch in `Cron.hs:617-626`, where it calls `reconcileProviderEvents` and `markSourceSuccess`. The stale response can therefore increment `missing_runs`, potentially hide an event that had already missed one run, and record the disabled source as successful; propagate this failure or recheck/lock source enablement around reconciliation and the success update.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in a125a347cacb8d941a515171e2a81d4c92f2c2d2. Per-event persistence errors now propagate (rescuing that change from PR464 commit 5068a0d with contributor attribution), preventing reconciliation and false success. Completion rechecks and locks the source before absence reconciliation, including empty responses; reconciliation, run completion and source success commit atomically. No network fetch occurs under the lock. Real PostgreSQL tests verify disabled empty-feed rejection with no success writes, forced final-write failure rolls back run completion, and enabled completion commits both timestamps. The existing mixed-capacity/concurrent writer/authority/revocation/rollback tests and 28 discovery examples pass; the actual Cron dependency graph compiles. No production constraint or validation was weakened.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Point the migration at an ancestor of this release**

Fresh evidence for the requested release SHA `39120b84ac361cc1498c7b4d32c073bc440eb503` shows that `git merge-base --is-ancestor 441dfcc968559f829e84c89751f008657566138c 39120b84ac361cc1498c7b4d32c073bc440eb503` exits 1: this commit has sole parent `648f2d6dc69080d4438ae2a25309497012ded2d1`, unlike the repaired branch head mentioned in the earlier thread. Consequently, `requireMigrationIntroductionAncestor` in `scripts/lib/production-release.mjs` rejects planning or deploying this exact release before the migration can run; record an introduction commit in this release's ancestry or preserve the repaired branch ancestry in the reviewed release commit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
